words.gloss: those who do not value their lives

literal: Desiring spreading fame, those who do not desire life, their fastening of the hero's anklet is of the nature of beauty.
translation: For those who desire resounding fame and disregard their own lives, the fastening of the hero's anklet is a fitting ornament of true beauty.
modern: உலகெங்கும் பரவும் புகழை விரும்பி, தம் உயிரைப் பொருட்படுத்தாத வீரர்களுக்கே, காலில் வீரக்கழல் கட்டுவது அழகைத் தரும் தன்மையுடையதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the true meaning of military adornments. The 'kazhal' is a traditional anklet worn by Tamil warriors to symbolize bravery. The poet explains that wearing this anklet is truly beautiful and meaningful only for those brave soldiers who seek resounding fame ('culalum icai') and are willing to sacrifice their lives ('vēṇṭā uyirār') on the battlefield. For anyone else, wearing it would be a hollow gesture without real substance.
